body:
Triage: card shape completed — a `needs-user-decision` card must carry the four-prong block at filing time; adding it now so the maintainer can rule without reconstruction. Type set to Bug (the severe half violates declared behavior: a 200-acknowledged Studio rename that no derived read serves). `domain:metadata` confirmed (mechanism is `packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts` + the metadata read seam, but the ruling is about read-surface semantics, decided here and implemented where the fold lives). Human floor applies — protocol/read-contract behavior change in both candidate directions — so no auto-adjudication; this is analysis, not a ruling.

**Four-prong block:**
1. **Platform long-term coherence:** "catalog loses to an explicit override" converges three read surfaces on one truth and gives scalars a provenance axis the fold already needs (this card is the sixth 200-means-nothing instance in the lane); "reconcile the diagnostic" leaves two truths standing and documents the divergence instead of removing it. First option shrinks the special case; second entrenches it.
2. **Measured business pull:** real and current — a tenant's ordinary Studio rename (`PUT /meta/object/:name` → 200) is silently discarded on every read a form derives from. Measured live on a deployment-shaped boot, not speculative. The extension-scalar half is milder but rides the same mechanism.
3. **AI-agent error-resistance:** a 200 whose effect is unobservable is the single worst shape for agent authors — an agent verifying its own write reads back the old value and loops or "fixes" the wrong layer. Explicit-override-wins makes the write observable; the repro pins in `showcase-object-extension-scalar-divergence.dogfood.test.ts` are already inverted (`it.fails`) to flip on the fix.
4. **Startup scope discipline:** provenance-through-the-fold is bounded work — three scalars, one mechanism, enumeration already landed (PR #8258); arm B ("fold drops scalars") is measured as a regression in disguise and is off the table by the dev's own reverse-verification. The cheap-looking alternative fixes the diagnostic, not the tenant.

**Recommendation:** catalog loses to an explicit override (carry scalar provenance through the fold); reconcile the `?layers=true` diagnostic only as a consequence, not as the fix. Prongs 2 and 3 point the same way and prong 4 does not veto. ⚠️ Read together with #8268 (`nameField`, same last-writer-wins scalar class) before ruling — one ruling can cover both shapes.

## Maintainer ruling — catalog loses to an explicit override (comparison-based provenance)

Ruled by the maintainer in a live PM session, 2026-08-13 (session `session_015XyMgCSMGGn9oSwbQEeWYg`), verbatim: 「其他全部接受你的建议。」 — accepting the recommendation as presented.

**Ruling:** the i18n catalog is the packaged translation of packaged defaults; a tenant's explicit scalar (their Studio rename that answered 200, or an extension overlay scalar) is authored data and **must win**. Implement via **comparison-based provenance** — the catalog value applies **only when the document's scalar still equals the packaged base value**; a scalar that differs from base has been explicitly set, and the catalog yields. No provenance flags carried through the fold. The edge (tenant renames to exactly the base value) degrades to a no-op, which is harmless. `?layers=true` stays untranslated and diagnostic, unchanged.

**Implementation notes for dispatch:**
- Mechanism lives in `packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts` (`catalog ?? document` precedence) with the base value reachable from the fold enumeration landed in PR #8258 — hence the domain relabel to `domain:spec` (anchoring rule: the fix lands in `packages/spec`; this supersedes the earlier `domain:metadata` routing).
- Covers all three scalars (`label`, `pluralLabel`, `description`) — one mechanism, per the card's enumeration.
- ⛔ Arm B (fold drops scalars) stays rejected — it deletes a documented `ObjectExtensionSchema` feature and leaves the tenant-rename defect untouched.
- The repro pins are already on `main` (`showcase-object-extension-scalar-divergence.dogfood.test.ts`, two `it.fails` cases): **inverting them to plain green is the acceptance signal** — ⛔ do not "repair" them any other way.
- Read together with #8268 (`nameField`, same last-writer-wins scalar class, in flight) — serial-check against it at claim time.

Label swap: `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue`; `domain:metadata` → `domain:spec`.

**Unlock sweep: blocker cleared.** `pm:blocked` → `pm:queue`.

Declared blocker: objectstack#8460 — verified **closed** against the GitHub API on 2026-08-14. No other blocker is declared on this card.

⚠️ **This card's `Blocked-by:` line lives in a comment, not the body.** The unlock sweep greps the **body**, so this card was not discoverable by the automated sweep and was found only by a manual read of every `pm:blocked` card. Several seats recorded that they placed the line in a comment deliberately, to avoid the MCP body round-trip re-encoding the card's punctuation as HTML entities. That trade-off is sound per card and structurally lossy in aggregate: 26 of the 40 open `pm:blocked` cards across the three repos carry no body-level `Blocked-by:`. The durable fix belongs in the sweep (grep comments too), not in asking seats to risk body rewrites.

**Closing as completed — both halves are delivered on `origin/main`** (spec seat, session `session_01E5tUwGM3LQoqErTfkvRW7W`, post-unlock premise re-verification).

The unlock sweep returned this card to `pm:queue` this morning after #8460 closed. Re-verifying the card's file surface on the merged ref shows the remainder was not merely unblocked — it was **implemented by the very merge that closed the blocker**:

1. **Catalog half** — PR #8454 (`Part of #8284`), MERGED 2026-08-13: comparison-based provenance; the first repro pin inverted green; three reads converge for extension-scalar cases.
2. **Fold-precedence half (the severe one)** — #8460's implementation PR #8620 (`01a7337`), MERGED: a tenant's rename beats a package extension's scalar in the object fold. That PR touched `showcase-object-extension-scalar-divergence.dogfood.test.ts` directly, and on current `origin/main` **both former `it.fails` repro pins are flipped to plain `it`** — including "SHOULD: a tenant's own rename reaches the reads its forms derive from" and "[#8284] after the rename the three reads still AGREE". Exactly the inversion this card's own Reproduction section named as the fix signal.

Nothing in the card's scope table remains unaddressed: the scalar mechanism was fixed at the fold (one mechanism, all three scalars), not per-key. Label cleaned to terminal state and the stale claim assignee cleared in the same stroke (the claiming session stood down 2026-08-14T05:4xZ; per-claim provenance is in the thread above).
